**Statement S1:**
In case of bit-interleaved parity, a single parity bit is enough for error correction.

This statement is true because in bit-interleaved parity, data bits are interleaved with parity bits. Each parity bit covers an entire block of data bits. Since the parity bit covers the entire block, a single parity bit can be used to correct errors in the entire block.

**Statement S2:**
In case of block level striping with N disks, block i of a file goes to disk (i mod N).

This statement is false because in block-level striping, each block of the file is divided into N parts, and each part is written to a different disk. The block number (i) is used to determine which disk each part goes to, not the remainder of i mod N.

**Statement S3:**
Block-interleaved parity involves keeping an entire parity block on a separate disk.

This statement is true because in block-interleaved parity, each parity block is stored on a separate disk. This is because each parity block covers an entire block of data, and storing it on the same disk as the data would not provide any error correction benefits.
